 Mitchell calls Wellington surface a ‘trampoline’
 By: Agencies 
 Date:
 November 8, 2026 
 Share post:
 WhatsApp Facebook X ReddIt Telegram Linkedin 
 WELLINGTON, Nov 7: New Zealand batter Daryl Mitchell described the Wellington surface as challenging after the hosts were bowled out for 134 in the second ODI against India, citing unpredictable bounce and difficulties in rotating the strike.
Mitchell, who top-scored with 55 off 104 deliveries, said the ball was coming through at varying heights, making it difficult for batters to judge their shots.“It’s pretty challenging out there. Obviously, we’d always like a few more, but yeah, it’s like batting on a trampoline at times. We weren’t quite sure what height the ball was going to come through at,” Mitchell said after the New Zealand innings.The right-hander also pointed to the difficulty of finding gaps and running quick singles, explaining that the nature of the drop-in surface made it harder for batters to rotate the strike.
“All of us found it really hard to rotate the strike as well. Being a drop-in pitch, it just stops. So you add that to the bounce and sometimes the best option was to try and give it a hit and see what happens,” he added.
The surface continued to challenge the batters throughout the innings, with the New Zealand players unable to establish consistent partnerships or build a substantial total. (Agencies)
